newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Ecopetrol confirms leadership changes.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Ecopetrol confirms leadership changes.

text.p: Colombia's state oil company, Ecopetrol, confirmed Tuesday that three members of its board of directors had resigned amid a controversy stemming from British Petroleum Co's demands for more profitable concession terms in its Piedemonte exploration contract.
An Ecopetrol spokesman said the three board members, including 10-year veteran Jose Fernando Isaza Delgado, resigned Monday but declined to comment when asked about the reason for their departure.
Isaza told the Bogota daily El Espectador that he had been forced to step down because of his opposition to a possible sweetening of BP's Piedemonte contract.
"I feel like I was pressured to resign," he said, adding that he had resisted calls on the government to bow to BP's demands.
Under the sliding-scale formula that currently applies to the Piedemonte contract, BP's profits are divided equally with Ecopetrol when total production is less than 60 million barrels.
The state share increases to a top rate of 70 percent when total production reaches 150 million barrels.
Piedemonte has estimated reserves of about one billion barrels of natural gas liquids and 10 trillion cubic feet of natural gas in the Pauto, Florena and Volcanera discoveries.
BP has argued that the sliding scale formula makes exploitation of Piedemonte economically unviable and Ecopetrol has officially said that it was considering improving the concession terms.
